# Determining \(\aleph_1^{\aleph_0}\)

## Setting Up the Bounds

The expression \(\aleph_1^{\aleph_0}\) represents the cardinality of the set of all functions from a countably infinite set to a set of cardinality \(\aleph_1\). I'll determine this by finding both a lower and upper bound.

**Key fact:** By Cantor's Theorem, \(2^{\aleph_0} > \aleph_0\), so \(2^{\aleph_0}\) is uncountable. Since \(\aleph_1\) is the *smallest* uncountable cardinal, we have:
$$\aleph_1 \leq 2^{\aleph_0}$$

## Lower Bound

Since \(2 \leq \aleph_1\), monotonicity of cardinal exponentiation gives:
$$2^{\aleph_0} \leq \aleph_1^{\aleph_0}$$

## Upper Bound

Since \(\aleph_1 \leq 2^{\aleph_0}\), monotonicity again gives:
$$\aleph_1^{\aleph_0} \leq (2^{\aleph_0})^{\aleph_0}$$

Now I simplify the right-hand side using the cardinal exponent law \((\kappa^\lambda)^\mu = \kappa^{\lambda \cdot \mu}\):
$$(2^{\aleph_0})^{\aleph_0} = 2^{\aleph_0 \cdot \aleph_0} = 2^{\aleph_0}$$

(The last equality uses \(\aleph_0 \cdot \aleph_0 = \aleph_0\).)

Therefore:
$$\aleph_1^{\aleph_0} \leq 2^{\aleph_0}$$

## Combining the Bounds

$$2^{\aleph_0} \leq \aleph_1^{\aleph_0} \leq 2^{\aleph_0}$$

By the Cantor–Bernstein–Schröder Theorem:

$$\aleph_1^{\aleph_0} = 2^{\aleph_0}$$

> **Remark:** Whether \(2^{\aleph_0} = \aleph_1\) (i.e., the Continuum Hypothesis) is independent of ZFC. So the most precise determination in ZFC is that \(\aleph_1^{\aleph_0}\) equals the cardinality of the continuum, \(2^{\aleph_0}\).

$$\boxed{2^{\aleph_0}}$$
